key_insight: Generated video alone gives robots motion, but not the force needed for real contact tasks. This paper shows that adding generated audio—especially sound loudness—can help infer a time-varying force profile for more realistic, force-aware manipulation.
problem_solved: Existing zero-shot manipulation methods based on video generation produce kinematic trajectories only, which often fail in contact-rich tasks because they ignore the forces required for safe and successful interaction.
method: Use video generation to obtain manipulation trajectories from visual demonstrations or prompts.
Augment the generated video with contact audio to estimate a bounded, time-varying desired-force signal from sound loudness.
Combine motion and audio cues in a pipeline that supports zero-shot, force-aware robot manipulation and can also generate training data for contact-rich tasks.
impact: This matters because many real-world robotics tasks depend on how hard, when, and where a robot pushes, presses, or touches—not just where it moves. The approach could improve robustness in manipulation and reduce the need for manually collected force-labeled data.

paper_title: Dreaming the Sound of Contact: Leveraging Video and Audio Generation for Zero-Shot Force-Aware Manipulation and Data Generation
paper_authors: Guanhua Ji, Tianyu Li, Dayoon Suh, Yuqian Zhang, Boyan Zhang
